## Objective

Implement coherent Curator project operation and functional ontology in the Sys4AI depot root, distribute complete neutral specialization capability, and deliver both through every supported selected setup route while resolving root health findings through current owners.

User value: A selected project gains usable, discoverable Curator functions and clear owner/authority rules without losing its existing knowledge, history, identity or operating choices.

### Success outcomes

- The active Sys4AI depot root shall expose one coherent project-local Curator process through its governance, charter, configuration, owner entry points and ontology, using the root's actual project identity and current operating policy.
- The ontology shall represent the supported Curator process and its meaningful functions, including policy inspection, scoped review, owner-routed update and correction, exact retry/recovery, Task pause/resume, selected dispatch, session catch-up and bounded log access.
- Curator ontology knowledge shall connect the process to project identity, governing skills and roles, Task lifecycle/current ownership, memory, ontology and maintenance obligations, with typed relationships and inspectable source provenance.
- Reusable source collections and the registered Sys4AI Template shall contain the complete Curator project and ontology capability needed for destination specialization through the supported initializer.
- Supported Sys4AI new-project creation shall deliver Curator project wiring and its functional ontology integration together as part of the same successful initialization workflow.
- First-time Sys4AI preparation of a selected existing project shall supply the same integrated Curator process and ontology functionality while preserving the destination's established identity, authored content and explicit configuration choices.
- Sys4AI shall provide a supported explicitly selected adoption or refresh route that completes Curator project and ontology integration for previously initialized projects, including those with an earlier Curator installation that lacks ontology integration.
- Integration setup and adoption shall preserve authored ontology and memory, Task history, project identity, licensing, custom packages, unrelated roles and explicit opt-outs, with exact change boundaries and recoverable operations.
- Curator project behavior and ontology representation shall consistently describe bounded session-start/return collection, subsequent current-owner evaluation and separately authorized execution, preserving the configured session-only operating mode.
- The root's pending Curator catch-up obligations identified by the health report shall receive current-owner disposition based on fresh bounded evidence and current source/ownership checks.
- The reported staged response under the cancelled historical Curator Task shall be investigated through the Task owner, with any lifecycle or native-write-ownership mismatch reconciled before a supported recovery or cleanup disposition.
- The root health follow-up shall establish actual local browser behavior for the selected on-demand ontology workbench and report its operating state accurately without requiring an always-on service.
- The integration and report follow-up shall preserve the working root memory retrieval, ontology core/backend behavior and their independent data, configuration and authority boundaries.
- Final integration reporting shall cover root, reusable sources, neutral Template and each supported initialization/adoption route, relating every requirement and health finding to current evidence and explicit limits.

## Scope

### In scope

- All 14 approved TRD requirements and 34 exact acceptance clauses.
- Reusable ontology/Curator semantics and owner interfaces, checked neutral Template distribution, new creation, first preparation, manual-copy specialization and explicitly selected historical adoption.
- Root exact package/ontology adoption, representative actual owner maintenance, pending obligation disposition, historical staged Task owner investigation, separately authorized on-demand browser observation and preserved memory/ontology health.
- Focused schema/query/setup/recovery/guard controls and classified final evidence across each route.

### Out of scope

- Executing any planned work during this planning operation.
- Bulk or unselected product-project adoption; creating a real destination or changing historical setup editions without its separate selected request.
- Restoring the rejected TRD; changing the approved source or dated health report.
- New background AI, unattended scheduler, service/hook installation, package/model/runtime provisioning, Git operations, external publication/deployment and external messages.
- Inventing actors or publication grants; replacing authored graphs, core imports, memory/Task schemas, existing receipt/history or independent configuration merely to pass checks.

### Execution authority

The current explicit Task and to-implementation-plan invocation authorizes plan creation and tracking only. It does not authorize implementation, installation, deletion, canonical ontology/memory/Task recovery, service startup, destination adoption, Git publication or any other separately governed action. A future exact-plan execution request must supply its actual selected scopes and owners.

### Constraints

- Planning creates no implementation authority. Exact managed draft revision approval is still required before ready; implementation, owner publication, service start and selected destination adoption retain separate gates.
- All planned operation and fixture verification results are future work; plan tasks remain planned and requirements active with no execution evidence.
- Use root .venv Python 3.12 standard library for core tooling. No dependency/model/runtime/service provisioning is in scope.
- Source collections own reusable changes; only checked Template mapping distributes automatically. Active root and ordinary projects remain separately selected.
- Current core loader imports sys4ai-core only; neutral starter graphs remain empty. The proposed recipe is reference data rendered to existing supported project-local ontology records.
- Real actor observations and current grants cannot be manufactured from JSON, stored ontology, historical Task/memory or fixture IDs.
- Preserve exact source, target, grant, native ownership and enabled guard checks at commit/recovery; rejected unknown input never grants repair/overwrite authority.
- No new Task, memory or setup ledger; any new integration owner evidence uses existing ontology control records and links through the existing setup receipt/history.
- The root has no generic project.json; its actual depot/configured identity is authoritative.
- Preserved path collections protect existing bytes/meaning/history and unselected children; explicitly named integration files, owner append-only receipts, selected disposable fixtures and their truthful registration evidence are the only later manifest exceptions. Every exception needs its current owning operation.
- Integration recipe edition 1.0.0, proposed governance-starter-v12 and versioned integration adoption records are distinct from the existing Curator runtime/configuration module_version 1.0.0. Existing configuration and historical operation records retain their original versions.
- Ordinary publication and configuration scopes are not widened. Existing authored installations use a new narrow ontology-owned integration-adoption operation with explicit exact config authority, current ownership and enabled-publication checks; a disabled required write remains a hold.
- No standalone manager, new service, generic migration framework or extra control-record store is introduced for integration. The existing setup owner links to the existing ontology owner transaction and verifies it before integrated setup completion.

## Decisions

| Decision | Status | Statement | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEC-001` | `approved` | Integrate Curator with the root project and ontology and supply the same complete functional integration through the neutral Template, new creation, first preparation and selected earlier-project adoption. | Approved TRD-20260913-C85981B3 revision 2 decisions and scope; requirement approval only. |
| `DEC-002` | `approved` | Retain Template neutrality, root/destination ownership separation, original setup editions and opt-outs; no bulk propagation or execution authority arises from TRD approval. | Approved TRD-20260913-C85981B3 revision 2 decisions and scope; requirement approval only. |
| `DEC-003` | `proposed` | Use ONTOLOGY-depo/integrations/curator/1.0.0 as a neutral declarative recipe, locator/manifest and competency resource, mapped to reference-assets/ONTOLOGY-depo/integrations/curator/1.0.0. A pure ontology-owned renderer produces separate destination-local graph, binding and competency files using existing project-local types and namespace rules. Keep active Template graphs empty, trusted context unchanged and sys4ai-core 1.0.0 locked. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
| `DEC-004` | `proposed` | Use stable destination namespace suffixes and local typed predicates where required; functions remain Capabilities linked to the installed curate Skill. Current owner roles/routes are sourced declarations, while current Task actor/authorization/outcome checks stay with their live owners. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
| `DEC-005` | `proposed` | Implement a narrow integration_preview/integration_publish/integration_recover API within the existing ontology owner for the reviewed Curator recipe. A distinct version-1 integrate-curator proposal/grant contract binds ontology.yaml additive file-list/allowlist selection plus the three exact integration files. It retains current owner, native observation, expiry, source, guard and immutable recovery checks; legacy publish proposals/grants and the core binding scope remain unchanged. Validate candidate config without writing or relaxing ordinary query/publication overrides. Root config adoption and semantic publication are one exact supported ontology-owner transaction, separate from root helper/resource adoption. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
| `DEC-006` | `proposed` | Propose governance-starter-v12 for new/first preparation and integration edition curator-ontology-1.0.0 in a version-2 project-curator module_adoptions operation. Keep existing Curator runtime/config module_version 1.0.0 and old operation schema/version meanings. New selected adoption uses prepare-existing --adopt-module curator; refreshing an earlier Curator installation explicitly adds --refresh-module curator (project-curator alias retained). An ordinary rerun or an unchanged completed adoption verifies its recorded edition. Refresh selects the current reviewed source inventory and records a new exact operation/history entry. Recheck version availability before implementation. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
| `DEC-007` | `proposed` | Preserve compatible authored ontology through additive reserved integration files and exact config selections. Current owner publication governs existing authored installations; missing authority or protected conflicts produces a named integration hold. Disabled settings remain unchanged, even when they prevent a requested write. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
| `DEC-008` | `proposed` | Use actual disposable setup operations with reopened results for representative route evidence, retaining their fixture limits. Root owner maintenance and workbench browser behavior require separate actual observations; no destination is invented as a live product and no service is started during planning. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
| `DEC-009` | `proposed` | Retain the separately authorized 128 MiB guard repair as prerequisite evidence only, including its one original setup fixture failure and later corrected installed dispatch results. Preserve active initializer v9 and root-specific Task helper/intake unless explicitly selected root adoption names them. New child setup uses the reusable source entry, observed at v11 before this proposed change; no guard capacity redesign is planned. | Senior synthesis grounded in both independent candidates and current inspected interfaces; this is a proposed plan choice pending exact canonical revision approval, with separate execution and action-specific authority required. |
